cases.source_text:
Synthetic dictation, authored for MediExtract testing. Not a real patient.

Forty-two year old gentleman here for review of his type two diabetes. Sugars
at home running high, fasting around nine to ten. Weight stable, no polyuria.
Feet examined today, sensation intact, pedal pulses present.

Plan: start metformin 500 mg po bid with meals, review in six weeks with
repeat HbA1c. Counselled on GI upset in the first fortnight. He denies any
drug allergies. Mother has hypertension on amlodipine.
cases.notes: mother's amlodipine is attribution, not the patient's medication

cases.source_text:
Synthetic dictation, authored for MediExtract testing. Not a real patient.

Fifty-eight year old lady, follow up hypertension. BP today 148 over 92,
repeat 144 over 90. She was on amlodipine 5 mg daily until March but stopped
it herself because of ankle swelling. Nil since.

Reports a rash to penicillin as a child, tolerates augmentin apparently, so
query the history. Father is on metformin for diabetes.

Plan: consider starting losartan if readings stay above 140 systolic at home.
Home BP diary for two weeks, review then. No new medication issued today.

allergy.value: Penicillin - childhood rash, but tolerates augmentin

cases.notes: amlodipine stopped in March, losartan only contemplated, metformin is father's
